paragraph: Park Ridge single-family is where the volume is, with 29 sales over six months at a median of $999,750 against a median list of $899,000. That is a sale-to-list ratio of 1.10, 93 percent of homes closing above asking, and a median of 13 days on market. This is a real seller's market, and buyers should expect multiple offer situations on anything well presented. Condos and townhouses are a much thinner tier at 10 sales, median $552,500, 23 days on market, and a 1.02 ratio. The range there runs from $390,000 to $1,820,000, so the median is the better guide than the average. Monthly counts are too small to read a clean trend, but volume built through June the way it usually does here, and July's single-family median of $921,000 on five closings is within the normal bounce. If Park Ridge follows the usual seasonal arc, expect closings and medians to ease through fall without much change in how fast well-priced homes go. If you're comparing tiers, the deciding factor isn't market heat. It's whether you want the space and grounds of a single-family or the low-maintenance lifestyle of a condo or townhouse.
